deep.reconstruction:
PART A (end of a note begun on the previous page). Hilbert wants the 'inner reason' why the discriminant of the Legendre polynomial (Kugelfunction) equals the reciprocal of the discriminant of the quadratic form ∫_{-1}^{1} f(x)^2 dx. That form is the Hankel form of the moments.

Setting (previous page). φ(z) is a polynomial with indeterminate coefficients. For each ν one determines polynomials A_ν, B_ν of degree ν such that A_ν φ + B_ν φ' is divisible by as high a power of z as possible. This is a two-point Hermite–Padé condition. After reversing z ↔ 1/z it becomes the condition that the combination have minimal degree. Between consecutive A_ν, A_{ν+1}, A_{ν+2} (and likewise the B's) there is a three-term linear recursion.

Claims on this page:
(i) The combinations A_ν φ + B_ν φ' are exactly the Sturm functions of φ. The last of them is the discriminant (resultant of φ and φ').
(ii) The recursion coefficients are polynomials (ganze rationale Functionen) in the coefficients of φ.
(iii) The theorems on reality of the zeros of the Legendre polynomials should follow from the same mechanism.
No computation is given; this is a research programme.

PART B (new topic): continued-fraction / Padé expansion of (1−z)^α.

1. Setup. Take N = N_n(z) of degree n and Z = Z_{n−1}(z) of degree n−1. Require
 f(z) = N(z)(1−z)^α − Z(z) = z^{2n} + a z^{2n+1} + ….
 Count (mine): there are 2n+1 unknown coefficients and 2n homogeneous linear conditions (coefficients of z^0 … z^{2n−1} vanish). So a nonzero solution exists. Z/N is then the [n−1/n] Padé approximant of (1−z)^α, i.e. a convergent of its continued fraction.

2. Goal. Find the 2nd-order linear ODE satisfied by f. The key point is to show it has no singular points besides z = 0, 1, ∞.

3. Method: differentiate and clear the factor (1−z). The correct formulas (mine) are:
 (1−z) f' = [(1−z)N' − αN](1−z)^α − (1−z)Z'
 (1−z)^2 f'' = [(1−z)^2 N'' − 2α(1−z)N' + α(α−1)N](1−z)^α − (1−z)^2 Z''.
 Thus each of f, (1−z)f', (1−z)^2 f'' has the form P_i(1−z)^α + Q_i with polynomials P_i, Q_i.

4. Eliminating (1−z)^α and the polynomial parts gives a 3×3 determinant relation (completed on the next page). It reads (1−z)^2 G f'' + … = 0, with
 G = P_0 Q_1 − P_1 Q_0 = −[(1−z)(NZ' − N'Z) + αNZ], up to sign.
 G has degree ≤ 2n−1.

5. Next-page argument (my justification). Put u = N(1−z)^α. Then
 W(u, Z) = (1−z)^{α−1}[(1−z)(NZ' − N'Z) + αNZ].
 Since Z = u − f, this equals f u' − f' u = O(z^{2n−1}).
 Hence G = c·z^{2n−1}. So the only finite zero of the leading coefficient is z = 0, and the ODE is singular only at 0, 1, ∞.
 Because the singularities are regular ('Riemann type'), f is a Riemann P-function (hypergeometric). This is Riemann's 1857 route to Gauss's continued fraction.

6. Explicitly (mine), N = 2F1(−n, α−n+1; −2n+1; z) and Z = 2F1(−n+1, −α−n; −2n+1; z).
 Example n = 1: N = 1+αz, Z = 1, f = −α(α+1)/2·z^2 + …, G = α(α+1)z.
errors: The first-derivative line as written, (1−z)f' = {(1−z)N' + N}(1−z)^α + Z'(1−z), is wrong in two ways. The N-term must carry −α: (1−z)N' − αN. The Z-term must have a minus sign: −(1−z)Z'.
The second-derivative line is left incomplete. Its correct bracket is (1−z)^2 N'' − 2α(1−z)N' + α(α−1)N, and the trailing term is −(1−z)^2 Z''.

Claim (i) holds only up to normalization. The Euclidean Sturm remainders agree with the subresultant sequence only up to rational factors. The final one equals the discriminant only up to a factor (a power of the leading coefficient and a constant), not literally.

Normalizing the z^{2n} coefficient to 1 is justified only afterwards (next page), by showing G ≢ 0, i.e. that the order of f at 0 is exactly 2n. This needs the generic α condition α ≠ −1, −2, …, which is not stated.

results.what: Sturm sequence of φ realized as the combinations A_νφ + B_νφ' with maximal order of vanishing; last term is the discriminant; three-term recursion with coefficients polynomial in the coefficients of φ
results.modern_name: Subresultant sequence / Sturm–Sylvester theory; Padé-type characterization of the Euclidean algorithm

results.what: Discriminant of the Legendre polynomial equals the reciprocal of the discriminant of the Hankel form ∫_{-1}^{1} f^2 dx
results.usually_credited_to: Stieltjes (1885) and Hilbert (1888, 'Über die Discriminante der im Endlichen abbrechenden hypergeometrischen Reihe')

results.what: Padé approximants of (1−z)^α via the 2nd-order ODE satisfied by the remainder f = N(1−z)^α − Z, with the Wronskian-type coefficient G = c z^{2n−1} showing singularities only at 0, 1, ∞
results.modern_name: Padé table of the binomial function; hypergeometric (Riemann P-function) characterization of Padé remainders; Gauss continued fraction

deep.surprise_reason: Both topics are classical. The Padé/continued fraction of (1−z)^α via a hypergeometric ODE goes back to Gauss, Riemann and Laguerre. Sturm sequences as subresultants go back to Sylvester. Hilbert's own 1888 discriminant paper already covers the Legendre/Jacobi discriminant. The page is a research sketch with a neat but standard Wronskian trick, worth noting as his working method rather than as a new result.

checkable.asserts: G for n=1 equals α(α+1)·z = c·z^{2n−1}.
Case n=2 with N = 2F1(−2, α−1; −3; z) = 1 + 2(α−1)z/3 + α(α−1)z^2/6 and Z = 1 − (α+2)z/3 [=2F1(−1, −α−2; −3; z)]: the expansion starts at z^4.
Case n=2: G = (1−z)(NZ'−N'Z) + αNZ is a constant multiple of z^3 (only zero at z=0, degree 2n−1).

transcription_corrections: In the formula f(z) = z^{2n} + a z^{2n+1} + …, the trailing 't...' is just '+ …'.

The first displayed derivative line in the image reads roughly '(1−z) df/dz = {(1−z)N + N'}(1−z)^α + Z'_?(1−z)'. The bracket is garbled (N and N' possibly interchanged) and the α factor is absent. The transcription's '{(1−z)N' + N}' is an interpretation; the mathematically correct content is {(1−z)N' − αN}(1−z)^α − Z'(1−z).
The second line in the image reads '(1−z)^2 d^2f/dz^2 = {(1−z)^2 N + N' − … )' with blanks left by Hilbert; the transcription's N'' is a plausible reading.
'Bz.' at the start probably abbreviates 'Bez.' (beziehungsweise) or 'Bzw.'; it is the continuation of 'Dieselbe besteht auch zwischen den B'.
'Wichtigste' and 'Differentialgleichung' are hyphenated across lines in the original.
